text: I run Eygentic. We help small B2B teams figure out what actually brings them customers.

And I have the same problem myself: working out who to reach out to this week. Lead lists give me thousands of names and no reason to call any of them. A chatbot gives me reasons, but I can't tell which ones are real.
Before this hackathon I had a rough prototype. This week I rebuilt it on Muse Spark. Here's what it does now.
I type in my website. That's the only thing it asks for.
First it reads my site and works out what I sell, who buys it, and what would make a company need us right now.
It looks up my competitors, and checks each one against their own homepage.
Then it looks for companies showing that need today. Open job posts on Lever, Greenhouse and Ashby, news, product launches.
It even reads a company's site code, so it knows if they already use a competitor.

Every quote it finds goes to a second model, Muse Spark Open on Baseten. That one can't browse. It only sees the quote and what it's supposed to prove, and it throws out anything that doesn't hold up.
say: Every quote it finds goes to a second model, Muse Spark Open on Base-ten. That one can't browse. It only sees the quote and what it's supposed to prove, and it throws out anything that doesn't hold up.

text: Here's a search I finished earlier.
ThriveCart made the shortlist.
Their job post says they're hiring one of the first three SDRs for a new enterprise push. That's exactly when a team needs us.
It drafts the first line of my email from that quote, and the second model checks it before I see it.
Storable looked like a good fit at first.
But their about page says they have over 800 employees, and we work with seed to Series A. So it's rejected, and it shows me why.
say: But their about page says they have over eight hundred employees, and we work with seed to Series A. So it's rejected, and it shows me why.

text: The models collect and check the evidence. The verdict comes from plain rules in code, so I can always see exactly why.
I can also see everything that got thrown out. Across my searches, that was about a third of all quotes.
If it can't prove something, the company goes to Needs a look, with what's missing.
No website yet? You can just describe what you sell.
This search covered five companies and cost 42 cents. And every quote links back to where it came from.
say: This search covered five companies and cost forty-two cents. And every quote links back to where it came from.

text: So now I know who to email this week, and what to say.
It's live. Try it with your own website.
